main_text.head: SECT. VI.
main_text.p: Et hæc Confirmatio, (βεβαίωσιν vocat ApostolusHeb. 6.16[?] loco jam dicto,) est ipsissimus Juramenti Finis. Nam cum res particulares incertæ essent & dubiæ ob earum contingentiam, nec possent probari nisi per testes, esset autem humanum omne testimonium valde infirmum & fallibile, ex duplici maxime defectu; Scientia, sc. (multa enim nos latent,) & Conscientia (cum sit Omnis homo mendax;Rom. 3.4) & tamen expediret hominibus, ut de rebus inter ipsos controversis & mutuo agitatis haberetur aliqua certitudo; qua sine nulla esset inter homines fides aut justitia, quæ sunt firmissima vincula humanæ societatis: necesse fuit recurrere ad testimonium Dei, qui nec fallere potest nec falli. Sicque receptum est apud omnes gentes, ex instituto Dei vi juris naturalis, velut huic malo congruum e remediumMaximum remedium expediendarum litium.l.1.ff. de jurejur. Maximum dirimendarum causarum remedium.l.3. Sed 8.Cod. de jurejur. Juramentum. Omnium judicio μεγίστη παρ' ἀνθρώπων πίστις, inquit Diodorus Siculus; & Dionysius Halicarnasseus τε-κμηρία[?] πίστις[?] & utroque elegantius major utroque Apostolus πάντης ἀντιλογίας πέρας[?] Heb. 6. Huc ubi ventum est, Ne plus ultra: si-stat se oportet omnis humana disceptatio & contradictio. Non quod omne quod jura-mento

page.notes: Uncertain: the first word of the page ("saret") is a fragment; the first letter is cut off, so the reading is doubtful. Greek words in the Diodorus and Dionysius passages and "πάντης ἀντιλογίας πέρας" are hard to read and are marked [?]. The Heb. 6 reference number is partly unclear and may be 16. The note for "e" is set in italic; the parts of the reference I could not check letter by letter are given as printed. Printed hyphens are kept as printed; "Sed" is read from a long-s form in the note.
